key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though defects create deep gap levels, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where device optimization should focus beyond point-defect passivation alone.
method: First-principles calculations on a large, chemically diverse set of point defects in trigonal selenium
Quantified defect-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall recombination via nonradiative multi-phonon emission and radiative capture
Compared recombination behavior across defect level position, lattice relaxation, charge state, and doping conditions
evidence_signal: The study evaluates a broad defect dataset and finds large lattice reorganizations plus energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, strongly suppressing SRH recombination.
watch_item: The conclusion is defect-specific and does not rule out other loss mechanisms, so device limits may still arise from interfaces, extended defects, or transport issues.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
